name: Overlook at Uplands
headline: St. Charles Town Company developed Overlook at Uplands, 247 new one- to three-bedroom apartments in seven buildings for households at 40% to 70% AMI on Clay Street in Westminster's Uplands master plan, with a 2023-cycle federal 4% credit, CHFA bonds and CHFA's largest-ever multifamily loan; it is now leasing.
why_it_matters: The first large affordable rental piece of the contested 234-acre Uplands redevelopment of former church farmland, financed through CHFA's CAPABLE bond-loan program with a $67.2M construction-to-permanent loan; it is now leasing.

status.label: Financing closed (2024); leasing as of October 2026
status.detail: CHFA reported its $67.2M construction-to-permanent loan in its September 2024 newsletter. As of 2026-10-21 the property's leasing website offers one- to three-bedroom homes with a move-in concession, and the City of Westminster lists it among its affordable rental communities. No public record found gives a certificate of occupancy date, and the deal is still on CHFA's 4% award report (no 8609s issued).

next_step: Watch for 8609 issuance (move to CHFA's 4% Completed Developments Report) and lease-up reports.

key_numbers.meaning: 77 one-, 130 two- and 40 three-bedroom units; 13 at 40%, 40 at 50%, 129 at 60% and 65 at 70% AMI (average about 60% AMI, computed).
Federal credit runs 10 years; amounts marked subject to change.
CHFA is the issuer per its award report; CHFA's 2024 newsletter cites $45,770,000 of private activity bonds.
Through CHFA's CAPABLE program; CHFA called it the largest multifamily loan in its history.

facts.value: 8775 Clay Street, Westminster 80031 (CHFA); leasing office at 8670 Clay Street
Family, new construction; in a QCT; not in a DDA or SADDA; Section 8 column marked No

Part of Uplands, a 234-acre, up to 2,350-home redevelopment of former Pillar of Fire Church farmland between Federal and Lowell boulevards and 84th and 88th avenues, approved by Westminster City Council 5-2 in December 2021

Pool and hot tub, splash pad, playground, dual basketball/soccer court, three barbecue areas, fitness center with yoga studio, clubroom, media room, business center; in-unit washer and dryer; carports and garages
The City of Westminster lists it as a St. Charles Town Co project of 247 units for households at 40% to 70% AMI

money.note: Cycle year 2023; amounts marked subject to change.
CHFA's 2024 newsletter gives $45,770,000. Whose bond cap is not stated publicly.
Largest multifamily loan in CHFA's history, per CHFA.

parties.role: Bond issuer, lender and credit allocator
parties.name: CHFA
Partnership including Oread Capital & Development, Varde Partners, Peak Development and Dream Finders Homes

background.text: Westminster City Council approved the Uplands master plan 5-2 in the early hours of 2021-12-21 after three nights of hearings; neighbors had fought to preserve the farmland.
The Uplands master developers broke ground on the overall site on 2023-09-27, with the governor attending and neighbors protesting at the entrance.

BizWest reported on 2024-04-08 that St. Charles Town Co. was scheduled to present its plans for several hundred apartments in Uplands to city officials, with a rendering taken from Westminster planning documents.
CHFA's September 2024 newsletter reported the CAPABLE loan, implying the financing closed by about August 2024 (inferred from the newsletter date).
The deal does not appear in CHFA's 2023 Round One or Round Two applicant reports or the 2023 Round Two award report.

discrepancies.text: CHFA's award report lists $43,640,000 of CHFA bonds, while CHFA's September 2024 newsletter cites $45,770,000 of private activity bonds.
CHFA lists the address as 8775 Clay Street, while the leasing website and the city's affordable rental list give 8670 Clay Street.

open_questions: Westminster site approvals for the parcel (official development plan, plat) with dates and resolution numbers; Westminster's planning commission minutes from 2024 were not reachable online.
Construction start and certificate of occupancy dates; groundbreaking coverage for this parcel (a 9News/Denver Business Journal report on construction starting was not reachable).
Whose private activity bond cap backs the CHFA bonds, and whether the bond amount is $43.64M or $45.77M.
Other public money: a $3,000,000 State Housing Board award for Overlook @ Uplands is indexed on DOLA's site, but the page returned an error and could not be verified.
Total development cost (reported elsewhere as about $89M, unverified), equity investor, general contractor, rents and affordability period.
